1.subject: Input parsers, template output contexts and typed SQL/OS/LDAP/XML operations
1.action: Exercise injection strings in each context; inspect escaping/parameterization; no unsafe interpreter path

2.subject: Schema/business validation, transactions and automation entry points
2.action: Use valid/invalid/raced/replayed transitions and enforce declared constraint without partial effect

3.subject: Browser cookies, origin policy, headers and UI storage
3.action: Capture real browser headers/cookie flags; simulate cross-origin/framing/cache/storage attack for requirement

4.subject: API routes, message parsers and realtime interfaces
4.action: Send malformed HTTP and protocol-specific requests with scoped foreign credentials; verify documented errors

5.subject: Upload scanner/parser/private storage and authorized download gateway
5.action: Use valid/malicious/oversized/traversal input and expired or revoked download scope

6.subject: Password/MFA/recovery/authenticator lifecycle across all actual login pathways
6.action: Test requirement-specific positive/negative authentication, rotation/reset/recovery, replay and rate boundary

7.subject: Session creation, reauth, expiry, logout and factor changes
7.action: Record cookie/session before and after expiry/logout/role change; reuse old token to verify denial

8.subject: Subject/tenant/router/object/action permission enforcement
8.action: Replay same action via UI/API/worker/export with valid, foreign, revoked and absent scope

9.subject: Any self-contained tokens, including signed actions if implemented
9.action: Inventory token types then mutate signature/algorithm/key/issuer/audience/time/type; reject invalid context

10.subject: OAuth/OIDC roles if introduced by approved ADR
10.action: Prove absence or test exact role flow including redirect/state/code/PKCE/issuer/audience/consent invariants

11.subject: Cryptographic inventory, KDF/encryption/RNG/key lifecycle
11.action: Inspect approved algorithms/config and exercise bad key/ciphertext/randomness/rotation failure paths

12.subject: Public/service-to-service TLS endpoints and certificate lifecycle
12.action: Attempt invalid/expired certificate, downgraded protocol, wrong hostname and untrusted service identity

13.subject: Deployment/service principal, secret provider and egress allowlists
13.action: Inspect runtime role/config; wrong/missing identity and forbidden egress must fail closed

14.subject: Personal/sensitive information inventories, client/server storage and retention
14.action: Query each classified location with valid and invalid scope; verify no prohibited residuals

15.subject: Architecture, dependency/attack-surface and defensive-code contracts
15.action: Review source/design/lockfiles and execute relevant parser/unsafe-deserialization/concurrency/error probes

16.subject: Security events, log integrity/redaction and safe errors
16.action: Trigger required event/failure; compare log scope/integrity/no secrets and client-safe response

17.subject: WebRTC/TURN/media/signaling if ever introduced by approved ADR
17.action: Prove absence or run authorized relay/media/signaling authentication and scope abuse cases

completion_steps: Apply every condition and numeric minimum in the pinned req_description to concrete implementation subjects; enumerate cases and freeze expected before run.
For candidate N/A, attach absence inventory and distinct reviewer approval; unexpected feature reactivates requirement.
evidence_required: positive/negative results or approved absence evidence

reference_resolution: Resolve same-document JSON Pointer refs; each exact ASVS row remains expected oracle, profiles describe common probes.
